title: Folic acid and folinic acid for reducing side effects in patients receiving methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis
authors: Shea B, Swinden MV, Tanjong Ghogomu E, Ortiz Z, Katchamart W, Rader T, et al.
population: Six double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trials in adults with rheumatoid arthritis taking methotrexate at up to 25 mg weekly, with folic or folinic acid at a starting dose of up to 7 mg weekly
funder: Internal sources: University of Ottawa, Clinical Epidemiology Unit; University of Ottawa, Institute of Population Health. External sources: no sources of support supplied.
result: Folic or folinic acid against placebo: gastrointestinal side effects 256 against 346 per 1000 (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.92; absolute reduction 9.0%; number needed to treat 11, 7 to 35; follow-up 24 to 52 weeks); transaminase elevation 48 against 208 per 1000 (RR 0.23, 0.15 to 0.34; absolute reduction 16.0%; NNT 6, 6 to 7; 8 to 52 weeks); withdrawal for any reason 98 against 250 per 1000 (RR 0.39, 0.28 to 0.53; absolute reduction 15.2%; NNT 7, 6 to 9; 8 to 52 weeks); stomatitis RR 0.72 (0.49 to 1.06). No statistically significant effect on the efficacy of methotrexate measured by joint counts and global assessments.
